Subject: RE: FOI "Llandough Roman villa & medieval house finds were destroyed in a 1983 fire"

Dear HER Team,

Thank you for your reply to my request of 24 September 2026 about the 1983 GGAT warehouse fire, surviving material and the custody of archaeological records. You say Heneb does not hold records pertaining to the requests in my email. New information has come to light about historical wordings, including “Llandough Home Farm” in the 1881 census. Please rerun or extend the relevant checks using the search terms below and identify the terms, collections and indexes checked, and anything newly identified within the original request.

Please retain the distinction in my original request between the 1978 - 79 Llandough Farm / Roman villa investigation and the separate Great House Farm site and its 1990 assessment and 1994 excavation. The Great House Farm site is beside St Dochdwy’s Church, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Penarth and Cardiff: HER GGAT02038s, NPRN 20182, grid reference ST16707335, later Church View Close, [postcode redacted]. The different Llandough near Cowbridge is outside scope.

Farm and building search forms: “Great House Farm”, “Great House Farm, Llandough”, “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”, “Great House”, “Great house”, “Greathouse”, “Tŷ Mawr”, “Ty Mawr”, “Ty-mawr”, “Ty Mawr Farm”, “Ty Mawr (Great House)”, “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”, “Cydfin Farm”, “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, “Cedfin”, “Cydwin”, “Cedwyn”, “Cedfyn”, “Cefin”, “Llandough Home Farm”, “Land Doc Home Farm”, “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”, “Llandough Church Farm”, “Church Farm”, “former Great House Farm”, “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church” and “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”. Related descriptions include “an 800-year-old house”, “the ten-roomed house”, “ancient Welsh house” and “the farm / the whole of the farm”.

The checked 1881 census page reads “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm” is a competing reported transcription and “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm” is a reported lead not appearing on that page. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are unverified research leads; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Church Farm” and “Llandough Church Farm” are source-specific terms whose identity is unresolved. The 1994 Ideal Homes Wales plan uses “LLANDOUGH FARM” for the development site, while the Rees family Llandough Farm is a separate farmstead. A shared wording alone does not establish that records refer to the same place.

Estate and associated-place terms: “Cedwyn Estate”, “Cydwin”, “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” and “Cwm Cydfin Wood”. Cedwyn Estate is the family's working name, not an established period name. The Bute catalogue's 1552 - 1824 range is not a specific date for the Ty Mawr wording; the 1824 Stewart survey records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, and a 1902 sale catalogue names Cwm Cydfin Wood. These terms do not establish common boundaries or title.

Locality search forms: “Llandough-juxta-Penarth”, “Llandough near Penarth”, “Llandough near Cardiff”, “Llandough, Penarth”, “Llandough, Cardiff”, “Llandough”, “Landoche-juxta-Cardif”, “Llandough / Leckwith”, “Penarth Road, Llandough”, “Urban District of Penarth”, “Llandochau”, “CF64” and “Church View Close, [postcode redacted]”. Landoche-juxta-Cardif is a manor locator and Llandough / Leckwith is neighbouring parish and manorial context.

From: Requester <[email redacted]>

Subject: Casework archive enquiry - Tŷ Mawr (Great House Farm), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan (1988)

Dear Historic Buildings & Places,

I am researching the history of Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan (approx. ST 168 733), the house beside St Dochdwy's Church. The family's recorded transcription of the index to an 1824 Bute estate survey (Glamorgan Archives, DB/E/1, plan 19) gives the name "Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm". The house was demolished in late 1988. The South Wales Echo of 3 December 1988 ("History fight to save farm") reported that Cadw was considering spot-listing the farmhouse and that an inspector was due to visit that weekend.

As the Ancient Monuments Society was a national amenity society for England and Wales at that time, please could you tell me whether the Society's casework records include anything about the house, for example:

1. any notification, request for spot-listing, or correspondence about its threatened demolition in 1988–89; or
2. any earlier record of the building.

If such records exist, I would be grateful for a reference and a short description, and to know whether they are held by the Society or have been deposited with an archive.

I would welcome a short acknowledgement.

Kind regards,

Requester
